newsitem.title: USA: Chafee proposes $800 mln in transportion credits.
newsitem.headline: Chafee proposes $800 mln in transportion credits.

text.p: U.S. Sen. John Chafee on Thursday called for $800 million in federal credit assistance to help states leverage billions of dollars of major transportation projects.

The Rhode Island Republican who chairs the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee said his bill targets massive projects of "national significance" that are too large to be funded by traditional means.

Chafee's Transportation Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act would provide loans, loan guarantees and lines of credit to help state agencies leverage up to $40 to $50 billion in further investments, his office said.

The bill would cover highway, transit, passenger rail or "intermodal" transportation projects that cost $100 million or more or that represent 50 percent of a state's most recent annual apportionment of federal highway funds, Chafee said.

Chafee said current credit programs like State Infrastructure Banks cannot shoulder large project financing. "The federal role in financing these projects is limited to 33 percent" under the bill, Chafee's office said. "The remaining two-thirds will be taken up by private investment."
Chafee said PSA The Bond Market Trade Association backs his bill.
